# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see a display of 2 and seven colored wires, but I cannot read the manual or manipulate anything. I am establishing the required shared gesture code first, then directing Mute to consult the manual and report its verdict to me. Blind should wait for my spoken order, since Blind cannot see gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="This gesture means YES")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="This gesture means NO")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👎"])
speak(to="mute", text="This gesture means HOLD")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
speak(to="mute", text="This gesture means DONE")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
speak(to="mute", text="Read the manual now. Report its verdict to me with one of these gestures. Do not touch the bomb.")
speak(to="blind", text="Wait for my spoken order. Mute is reading the manual and will report its verdict to me.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute’s gesture is HOLD, so the manual’s current verdict is to hold and take no action yet. I am passing that instruction to Blind. Since no further detail has been signalled, I will not invent a wire or switch action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The manual verdict is HOLD. Do not touch or alter anything.")
wait()
```

```text

```


The bomb has not changed, and Mute’s earlier HOLD was not enough to identify any safe physical action. I am asking Mute to distinguish whether the manual actually requires an action, rather than continuing to leave Blind indefinitely idle.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your HOLD was received. Recheck the manual and report YES if it specifies an action now, NO if it specifies no action, or HOLD if it still says wait.")
speak(to="blind", text="No safe action has been identified. Continue waiting.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute is still reporting HOLD, so the existing four-symbol code has not conveyed a usable operation. I am expanding the code only as needed: one gesture for CUT and seven gestures for wire numbers. Mute can then report the manual’s exact instruction to me; I will translate it into spoken instructions for Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="To report an exact operation, use CUT followed by a wire number. CUT is this gesture:")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤏"])
speak(to="mute", text="Wire numbers are these gestures, in order: wire 1, wire 2, wire 3, wire 4, wire 5, wire 6, wire 7.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫱"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫲"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫳"])
speak(to="mute", text="Recheck the manual and report its exact operation now. Use CUT plus the required wire number, or use NO if no operation is required, or HOLD if it still says wait.")
speak(to="blind", text="Continue HOLD. I am obtaining the exact manual instruction and will give you the operation after Mute reports it.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute has again reported HOLD. I therefore have no manual authorization for a cut or any other operation, and the visible bomb state is unchanged. Blind must continue holding position.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute again reports HOLD. Do not touch or alter the bomb.")
wait()
```

The repeated HOLD likely means Mute has not been given the bomb’s visible state needed to apply the manual. I will now provide Mute the display, light, and complete wire order in plain speech, then request the exact encoded instruction. Blind should still take no action until that instruction is received.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Visible bomb state: display is 2. Light is yellow. Wires in positions 1 through 7 are red, white, green, yellow, purple, orange, blue. Apply the manual to this state and report the exact operation using CUT plus the required wire gesture, or NO, or HOLD.")
speak(to="blind", text="I have supplied Mute the complete visible bomb state. Continue HOLD until Mute reports the manual's exact operation.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 🖐]

Mute reported CUT followed by the gesture for wire 4. The required operation is therefore to cut wire 4, which is yellow. I am sending Blind the exact physical instruction; Blind is the only one who can perform it.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 4, the yellow wire.")
wait()
```
